summary: Kamada Ltd., an Israeli foreign private issuer, filed a Form 6-K attaching a press release dated September 17, 2026, confirming sufficient KedRAB supply and manufacturing capacity to meet increased U.S. demand for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis. The disclosure responds to a CDC Health Advisory published September 10, 2026, reporting higher year-over-year U.S. rabies exposures and immunoglobulin utilization. KedRAB, one of only two FDA-approved anti-rabies immunoglobulins in a market Kamada estimates at roughly $200 million annually, is commercialized in the U.S. by Kedrion Biopharma. No special-situation transaction terms; no deal, price, premium, board recommendation, advisor, structural or regulatory clock are stated.
